title: The Linux Boot Process: Start to Services

scenes.say: Ever wondered what actually happens under the hood when you power on a Linux machine? Let's break down the boot process.

scenes.label: Firmware
scenes.sub: Runs POST, hands off to the bootloader
scenes.say: First, the firmware—BIOS or UEFI—runs checks and then hands control to the bootloader.

scenes.title: GRUB loads the kernel
scenes.say: The bootloader, usually GRUB, loads the kernel and its helpers, then the kernel wakes up your hardware.

scenes.label: systemd
scenes.sub: Starts as PID 1, manages all services
scenes.say: Next, the kernel launches systemd as process number one. systemd is the boss: it starts and watches over all your services.
systemd brings up the default target, like multi-user or graphical mode. Each service is defined by a unit file, and your own units live in the systemd settings folder.

scenes.question: What starts right after the kernel?
scenes.right: systemd starts as process one, then launches services and targets.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: What starts right after the kernel? It's not the login screen—it's systemd, which then brings up everything else.
